findings.claim: UntrustedData.MaximumObjectGraphDepth is raised tenfold from 500 to 5000 in a change that is about a generator/analyzer crash. This weakens a security default for every user of UntrustedData without opting in, and makes a stack overflow on deeply nested payloads more likely. The ledger notes a stack depth limit of 500 was deliberately kept, and it records no decision to raise it.

receipt_plan.detail: Deserialize a payload nested 600 levels deep (nested arrays) with MessagePackSecurity.UntrustedData. At base it throws InsufficientExecutionStackException. At head it succeeds. Optionally try 5000 levels on a small-stack thread to show a stack overflow.

findings.claim: The wrapper around reportDiagnostic now drops every analyzer diagnostic whose location is not in a syntax tree of the compilation. This includes diagnostics created with a null location (Location.None), for example MemberNeedsKey via FirstOrDefault()?.GetSyntax().GetLocation(). It also includes diagnostics that previously targeted other locations. Users could silently lose diagnostics they get today, such as MsgPack003/004/005 on locations that are not in source. The wrapper applies to all diagnostics, not just the crashing paths.

receipt_plan.detail: Run the analyzer test suite (MsgPack003/004/005/009 etc.) at base and head. Add cases where the diagnostic location is Location.None or comes from a partial or generic declaration in another tree, and compare which diagnostics are reported.
